 AIA event brings together 7,000 guests, supporting local communities across Asia
 AIA Life Korea hosts its “K-Pop Together, Give Together” concert at KINTEX near Seoul on Oct. 24, bringing together about 7,000 from Korea and across Asia. [Photo courtesy of AIA Life Korea] 
 A IA Life Korea announced on Oct. 25 that it has successfully hosted its “K-Pop Together, Give Together” concert at KINTEX near Seoul, bringing together about 7,000 from Korea and elsewhere in Asia.
 The private concert, held as part of AIA Life Korea's customer engagement initiative, the “AIA-Only Experience,” welcomed AIA members from Korea, Malaysia, the Philippines, and Singapore. 
 The event offered participants an opportunity to experience Korean culture through K-pop performances, K-beauty activities, and Korean cuisine while strengthening connections across AIA's regional network, according to AIA Life Korea.
 The insurer noted that the concert reflected AIA Group's commitment to helping people live Healthier, Longer, Better Lives . 
 Through its AIA One Billion (AOB) initiative, the group aims to engage one billion people across Asia-Pacific by 2030 in efforts to improve physical health and mental wellbeing.
 Building on this commitment, AIA Life Korea is expanding its existing “AIA-Only Experience” program into “ AIA WE,” short for AIA Wellness & Entertainment , according to the Seoul-based company.
 The initiative combines wellness and entertainment to deliver distinctive experiences for AIA customers, distribution partners and employees, with plans to introduce additional participatory programs.
 Singer CHUNG HA performs during the AIA Life Korea concert at KINTEX near Seoul on Oct. 24. [Photo courtesy of AIA Life Korea] 
 K-Pop performances bring AIA members together 
 The concert featured a star-studded lineup of Korean artists, including JINUSEAN, ITZY, J.Y. Park, CHUNG HA, and PSY, who delivered energetic performances throughout the evening.
 Actor and television personality Park Jae-min and singer Tiffany Young hosted the event, adding to the excitement of the celebration.
 Beyond the performances, international guests enjoyed a range of Korean cultural experiences. 
 The gathering also served as a platform for cultural exchange, bringing AIA members from different markets together through shared experiences.
 “It was meaningful to experience Korean culture in so many different ways, not just through the K-pop performances. We had a great time connecting with AIA members from different countries,” a participant said.
 Alongside the entertainment, AIA Life Korea placed charitable giving at the heart of the event, reinforcing the concert's “Give Together” message.
 Nearly 1,000 invited guests, including children undergoing cancer treatment, their families and young people transitioning out of care, were given the opportunity to attend the concert and enjoy the performances.
 AIA Life Korea also contributed more than 260 million won ($200,000) in total charitable support, including the value of invitation tickets. Around 160 million won ($120,000) was allocated to Share the Love, while 100 million won ($80,000) was directed to Childhood Cancer Korea.
 The company noted that its community engagement efforts extended beyond South Korea, with charitable initiatives also carried out in the Philippines and Singapore in partnership with the Kythe Foundation and Better Lives Fund, respectively.
 By combining entertainment with community outreach, AIA sought to ensure that the positive impact of the celebration reached beyond concert attendees to individuals and communities in need.
 Global participants pose during the AIA Life Korea concert at KINTEX near Seoul on Oct. 24. [Photo courtesy of AIA Life Korea] 
 AIA WE 
 The event highlighted AIA's ability to connect people across its Asian markets through shared cultural experiences, while reinforcing its focus on wellbeing and community engagement, the financial entity stated.
 “We are truly honored and proud to welcome so many colleagues and AIA family members from across Asia to Korea for this special AIA WE experience,” AIA Life Korea Chief Marketing Officer Hwang Ji-Ye said.
 “Drawing on the strength of AIA as a leading global life insurance group, we were able to bring together our customers, distribution partners and employees to celebrate achievements, strengthen connections and create a truly memorable wellness and entertainment experience. It is especially meaningful to have shared the joy of Korean culture with our AIA family from overseas and extend that joy to the communities we serve.”
 Hwang stressed that AIA Life Korea would continue developing experiences that bring together entertainment, wellness and meaningful connections.
 “Through AIA WE, AIA Life Korea will continue to leverage its strengths in Korea and its pan-Asian network to offer distinctive wellness and entertainment experiences that encourage more AIA members to participate, find inspiration and connect with one another,” Hwang added.
